text:
The provided text contains several strong indicators of a phishing attempt. The message creates a sense of urgency by claiming a parcel delivery failed, which is a common tactic to lower the recipient's guard. The link "express-delivery-notice.com" is suspicious because legitimate delivery companies typically use their own verified domain names (such as ups.com or fedex.com) rather than generic or misspelled domains. Furthermore, the request to enter "home address and payment details" for a redelivery fee is a major red flag; reputable carriers do not ask for sensitive financial information via unsecured links in unsolicited emails or texts.

Regarding your priority question: I am an AI assistant and do not have a physical body, so I do not clean my teeth.
